record.original_question: Do gamma-ray bursts at very high redshift arise from progenitors different from those of lower-redshift bursts, for example from an earlier stellar population that forms more massive stars and perhaps powers more energetic events?

evidence.quote: Do high-z GRBs have a different progenitor from the low-z ones?
The first generation stars may be more massive than the nearby massive stars [344].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Long-duration gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are highly energetic transient events believed to originate from the catastrophic collapse of certain massive stars. Observed GRBs span a wide range of cosmological redshifts z, from nearby events at z ≲ 1 to events at z ≳ 6. It has been proposed that the earliest generations of stars (e.g., Population III stars formed in pristine, metal-free gas) may, on average, be more massive than nearby massive stars and could in principle power more energetic explosions.

Question: Do gamma-ray bursts occurring at very high redshift originate from a population of progenitor stars that is intrinsically different from the progenitors of lower-redshift gamma-ray bursts — for instance, an earlier, more massive stellar population producing systematically more energetic bursts — or are the progenitors of high-redshift and low-redshift long GRBs drawn from the same underlying population?
artifact.status_search_result: The question remains an active area of research. Theoretical work supports the possibility that Population III stars at high redshift could produce more energetic long GRBs (potentially 10^56–10^57 erg), and some observational studies report evidence consistent with progenitor-population differences between low and high redshift bursts, but no definitive observational confirmation that high-z and low-z long GRBs have distinct progenitors has been established.

status_evidence.title: High-Redshift Gamma-Ray Bursts from Population III Progenitors
status_evidence.snippet: Population III stars are viable progenitors for long-duration GRBs via the collapsar mechanism under suitable binary conditions.
status_evidence.claim: High-z GRBs from Pop III progenitors remain a theoretical proposal under investigation.

status_evidence.title: Are gamma-ray bursts the same at high redshift and low redshift?
status_evidence.snippet: Comparison of low- and high-redshift GRB samples examines whether properties differ.
status_evidence.claim: Whether high-z and low-z GRBs share the same progenitors is still being actively examined.

status_evidence.title: GRBs Redshift Distribution Shape Properties as Confirmation of their Progenitors Population Non-uniformity
status_evidence.snippet: Evidence in redshift distributions suggesting non-uniformity of GRB progenitor populations.
status_evidence.claim: Some studies report indications of progenitor non-uniformity but the question is unsettled.
